glossary.definition: An electronic device that follows instructions to take in, process and output information.
glossary.example: A laptop is a computer you can carry and use for schoolwork.

glossary.definition: The physical parts of a computer you can see and touch.
glossary.example: The keyboard, mouse and screen are all examples of hardware.

glossary.definition: The instructions or programs that tell the hardware what to do.
glossary.example: A word processor and a game are both examples of software.

glossary.definition: A piece of hardware used to give information to the computer.
glossary.example: A keyboard and a mouse are input devices because they send data in.

glossary.definition: A piece of hardware that shows or gives out information from the computer.
glossary.example: A monitor and a printer are output devices because they show results.

glossary.definition: The screen of a computer that displays images and text.
glossary.example: She watched her essay on the monitor.

glossary.definition: A huge global network that connects computers so they can share information.
glossary.example: The internet lets you search for information and chat with friends far away.

glossary.definition: A program you use to look at and move around websites on the internet.
glossary.example: Chrome and Firefox are popular browsers.

glossary.definition: A way of sending and receiving messages over the internet, short for electronic mail.
glossary.example: She sent her homework to the teacher by e-mail.

glossary.definition: A named collection of information stored on a computer, like a document or picture.
glossary.example: He saved his drawing as a file called 'art.png'.

glossary.definition: A small portable device used to store and carry files between computers.
glossary.example: Take your project home on a USB flash drive.

glossary.definition: A software program used to create, edit and print text documents.
glossary.example: She used a word processor to type her letter.

questions.question: Which of these is a computer?
questions.explanation: A laptop is a computer. The others are not computers.

questions.question: The physical parts of a computer that you can touch are called ___.
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical, touchable part of a computer like the keyboard and screen.

questions.question: Programs that tell the computer what to do are called ___.
questions.explanation: Software is the program or set of instructions that tells hardware what to do.

questions.question: Which of these is an INPUT device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends data into the computer, so it is an input device.

questions.question: Which of these is an OUTPUT device?
questions.explanation: A monitor shows information from the computer, so it is an output device.

questions.question: The screen of a computer that shows images and text is called a ___.
questions.explanation: The monitor is the display screen of the computer.

questions.question: The huge global network that connects computers to share information is the ___.
questions.explanation: The internet is the worldwide network that links computers together.

questions.question: Which program do you use to look at websites?
questions.explanation: A browser (like Chrome or Firefox) lets you view and navigate websites.

questions.question: Sending messages electronically over the internet is called ___.
questions.explanation: E-mail (electronic mail) is sending messages over the internet.

questions.question: A named collection of information stored on a computer, like a document, is a ___.
questions.explanation: A file is a named collection of data, such as a document or picture.

questions.question: Which device lets you carry files from one computer to another?
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive stores files so you can move them between computers.

questions.question: Software used to type and edit text documents is a ___.
questions.explanation: A word processor is software for creating and editing text documents.
